blocks: ### T443 (found by T392, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/edit-hook/t392-results.md`: after T392's chunked byte read the reversal tripwire still read every byte of the feature's log on each Edit, `event-log-hooks` alone 29.4 ms (a pool worktree) and 28.3 ms (the clone) at the median, growing about 0.5 ms a MB, measured 2026-11-27 (T392's record))
### T443 Approach (checklist part A)

decisions.summary: A derived index of the log's PreToolUse Edit (path, old) rows, kept by the reader alone, answered with T392's chunked scan of the tail since it, from one open file via read_at; no guard message changes.
decisions.why: Performance work on every Edit's hook, which the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20, 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'); the tripwire's verdicts are held to the full read as the oracle (differential 0 of 1,937 cold, warm and grown) and no message changes.

decisions.summary: T383's screen and T392's full read become test-only code, the oracle the index is held to.
decisions.why: The full read is the behavior being replaced for speed; keeping it as the tests' oracle enforces that the replacement answers as it did. Nothing the GM asked for is removed.

decisions.summary: The index lives at <events dir>/reversal/<feature>.idx, a subdirectory so state-sync and measure/events.rs pass it over, named .idx so no jsonl filter takes it.
decisions.why: Where a derived file lives is a rendering choice inside the task; it keeps the index out of commits and out of the log readers, observed by reading both.

decisions.summary: One self-describing file: versioned header with dev, ino, covered and lengths, the two raw windows, then one row a line; any malformation is no index and a rebuild.
decisions.why: Format choice; every malformed form falls back to the full scan, so it cannot change a verdict.

decisions.summary: The index is tied to the open file's fstat (same dev and inode, covered at most the length) and both windows re-read byte-equal; any mismatch rebuilds by a full scan.
decisions.why: The mechanism that keeps the index's answer equal to the full read's for every change a writer makes; within the task.

decisions.summary: ACCEPTED LIMITATION, sub-case (a): the same file changed in place at the same or greater length with both 4 KiB windows equal and bytes between them changed; an index kept over it answers from the old rows and a reversal among the changed lines could be missed.
decisions.why: It narrows the tripwire's guarantee from 'every reversal the full read caught' (feature 375's arbiter, the plan's constraint 2) to every reversal on logs written as the tooling writes them. Not legitimate on cost: the ground that holds is purpose-defeat. Any tie that sees an arbitrary same-length change to bytes it does not read must read every covered byte on every Edit (a whole-prefix digest is exactly that), which is T392's full read again and the 28 to 29 ms this performance task (FR-013, the GM 2026-11-20) exists to remove; so honoring it literally means not doing the task. And it does not gut the tripwire's purpose: the ruling rests on the block's writer census as stated (every file of rust/, scripts/ and the Makefile naming l7r-events, events_dir or L7R_EVENTS_DIR, 23 files, searched for append(true), fs::write, rename(, set_len, File::create, >>, mv, sed -i, each hit read, observed 2026-11-27), which finds no writer that rewrites a log in place: the append, state-sync's >> and cp, refile's append and temporary-file rename, and retask, which never changes path or old. A hand or hostile rewrite of the log could already defeat the full read by deleting the line, so the limit adds no evasion the old code lacked. It is said in index.rs' module doc and pinned by a test. Not re-run by this review (no repository read); the census's space covers rust/, scripts/ and the Makefile only, so a writer elsewhere (a Python tool, a hook script outside scripts/) would be outside it - and its verb list omits a truncating rewrite onto the same inode (shell >, cp or fs::copy onto an existing file); noted, not a finding, because any such writer reaches this case only by keeping every byte up to covered at its offset in both windows while changing a path or old between them, which no writer of an append-only log does.

decisions.summary: ACCEPTED LIMITATION, sub-case (b): the log replaced by a different file that is given the freed inode's number on the same device, at least covered long, with both windows byte-equal and bytes between them different.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from (a), since the inode check is what a recycled number defeats. The length and window checks still stand against each replacing writer the census names: refile's write_back drops or moves lines, which shifts the tail window for any change before covered (and a change wholly after covered leaves the indexed prefix true); state-sync cps only a log the clone lacks, so an index exists for it only if the log was first deleted, and the copy would then need another clone's bytes to equal this clone's at both windows while differing between them; a rotation or new file differs in its head window from the old log's first bytes at any length (this review's inference, not the block's observation, as is the deletion premise for state-sync's cp). What remains is a coincidence of inode reuse and two 4 KiB byte-equal windows with differing middles, which no writer is shown to produce; closing it fully needs the same every-byte read as (a), so the same purpose-defeat ground holds and the limit is stated in the block as covering this sub-case too.

decisions.summary: The index keeps exactly the lines the full parse would match (UTF-8, holds "Edit", JSON after trim, ev PreToolUse, tool Edit, a path key, missing old as null); a string path compared as its one serde spelling at a row's start, any other parsed and compared as a value.
decisions.why: Equivalence to the oracle; the differential and the every-byte cut test hold it to the full parse.

decisions.summary: covered always ends after a newline; an unterminated last line is answered for this call but never stored.
decisions.why: Keeps the answer equal to the full read's on a log mid-append; within.

decisions.summary: The hook now writes the index on a rebuild and when the tail passes STALE, by a unique temporary file and a rename, removed on a failed rename; racing hooks lose at most one's work.

decisions.why: A content rule matching the tests' fixed close reason; the measured real rows are not matched. Part of fixing the defect the task names.

decisions.summary: Leave out plan-gate and task-add rows naming a <digits>-<slug> feature with no specs/ directory in the reading tree; none left out when the tree has no specs/ at all.
decisions.why: A content rule on the gates' own detail forms (plan.rs, task_add.rs) for a feature that does not exist in specs/. On the copy every slug it leaves out is a fixture's -x slug (449-x, 600-x, 444-x, 9001-x, as the block's left-out line measures), so it drops no filed feature's row. It is part of fixing the defect the task names: the audit counting the fixtures' rows as real firings.

decisions.summary: Accepted by the builder: a plan-gate or task-add row of a feature filed in another clone, not yet in the reading tree's specs/, would be left out until that tree syncs. The alternative, also requiring the fixtures' -x slug, was not taken.
decisions.why: Adjudicated here, not taken on the builder's word. On the measured log the rule drops no filed feature's row: every left-out slug is a fixture's -x slug. The case the builder accepted has not been observed, would be transient (it lasts only until the tree syncs), and announces itself, since the left-out line names every slug with its count, so a wrong drop shows by name. Like the check-closed rule's exact-reason match, it is the false-positive margin of a content rule, not a wrong outcome that occurs. It does not narrow 'count real firings, not fixtures' on any row that exists (constitution XIV v2.36.0: a defect is a wrong outcome, not a gap no reader sees). If a filed feature's slug ever shows in the left-out line, that is a defect to fix then.

decisions.summary: The tenth task-add quick-red row (451 T37, 2026-11-20) is a real refusal and stays counted; 9 left out.
decisions.why: Measured as a real firing of a filed feature, followed by a real QUICK_OK probe. Counting it is the correct outcome, not something carved out.

decisions.why: The 685 were read by detail and are all sessions' own reasons. The two freeze-ok rows cannot change a 100% rate, so they are a difference no reader of the audit would see, not a defect (constitution XIV, GM 2026-11-19).

decisions.summary: The 1,017 sync-with-main closing-owes rows stay counted, with a printed 'still counted' line. Separating fixture rows from real ones is deferred to T468, which lands before T22.
decisions.why: The guard's 8% rate may be wrong: it could be anywhere from 8% to 100%. So this is a known defect that this task leaves unfixed, and the ruling rests on three things. First, the deferral meets FR-009 and the fix-as-we-go rule (GM 2026-11-18). The block states why: no field or content of the row tells a fixture's row from a real refusal, the pid pairs separate only 20 of 1,017 (measured), and a separate signal (the event or run log's push runs by time) needs a measurement of its own. It files T468. It orders T468 before T22, the same point T444 itself must land by, so the defect is not carried past the step. Second, the audit does not hide the rows: it prints them by name as still counted, with their reason. Third, the blocker in the earlier BLOCKED text, a found-and-left of 'none' while this defect stood, is what changed. This text is the only changed part besides the closing-owes paragraph.

decisions.why: Each held only the unfilled section template, with no approach and no decision. Removing them decides nothing about scope, and T444's real section stands in its place.
